claim: In 2015, as part of the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology, a Registered Report was published describing how selected experiments from the paper 'Melanoma genome sequencing reveals frequent PREX2 mutations' (Berger et al., 2012) would be replicated.
source: In 2015, as part of the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology, we published a Registered Report (Chroscinski et al., 2014) that described how we intended to replicate selected experiments from the paper "Melanoma genome sequencing reveals frequent PREX2 mutations" (Berger et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract with citations to both the Registered Report (Chroscinski et al., 2014) and the original study (Berger et al., 2012).

claim: Cells stably expressing ectopic wild-type and mutant PREX2 were regenerated using the same immortalized human NRASG12D melanocytes as the original study.
source: We regenerated cells stably expressing ectopic wild-type and mutant phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate-dependent Rac exchange factor 2 (PREX2) using the same immortalized human NRASG12D melanocytes as the original study.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and describes the experimental approach taken in this replication study.

claim: Evaluation of PREX2 expression in newly generated stable cells revealed varying levels of expression among the PREX2 isoforms.
source: Evaluation of PREX2 expression in these newly generated stable cells revealed varying levels of expression among the PREX2 isoforms, which was also observed in the stable cells made in the original study (Figure S6A; Berger et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract with reference to data from both the replication and original study (Figure S6A; Berger et al., 2012).

claim: Varying levels of PREX2 isoform expression were also observed in the stable cells made in the original study.
source: Evaluation of PREX2 expression in these newly generated stable cells revealed varying levels of expression among the PREX2 isoforms, which was also observed in the stable cells made in the original study (Figure S6A; Berger et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim references Figure S6A from Berger et al., 2012, indicating citation-based evidence.

claim: Ectopically expressed PREX2 was found to be at least 5 times above endogenous PREX2 expression.
source: Additionally, ectopically expressed PREX2 was found to be at least 5 times above endogenous PREX2 expression.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by Western blot data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The monitoring of tumor formation of stable cells in vivo resulted in no statistically significant difference in tumor-free survival driven by PREX2 variants.
source: The monitoring of tumor formation of these stable cells in vivo resulted in no statistically significant difference in tumor-free survival driven by PREX2 variants, whereas the original study reported that these PREX2 mutations increased the rate of tumor incidence compared to controls (Figure 3B and S6B; Berger et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by statistical analysis of tumor-free survival data presented in the results.

claim: The original study reported that PREX2 mutations increased the rate of tumor incidence compared to controls.
source: The monitoring of tumor formation of these stable cells in vivo resulted in no statistically significant difference in tumor-free survival driven by PREX2 variants, whereas the original study reported that these PREX2 mutations increased the rate of tumor incidence compared to controls (Figure 3B and S6B; Berger et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim references Figure 3B and S6B from Berger et al., 2012.

claim: The median tumor-free survival was 1 week in this replication attempt.
source: Surprisingly, the median tumor-free survival was 1 week in this replication attempt, while 70% of the control mice were reported to be tumor-free after 9 weeks in the original study.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by survival data presented in Figure 3A.

claim: 70% of the control mice were reported to be tumor-free after 9 weeks in the original study.
source: Surprisingly, the median tumor-free survival was 1 week in this replication attempt, while 70% of the control mice were reported to be tumor-free after 9 weeks in the original study.

claim: The rapid tumor onset observed in this replication attempt, compared to the original study, makes the detection of accelerated tumor growth in PREX2 expressing NRASG12D melanocytes extremely difficult.

claim: Berger et al. sequenced the whole genome of 25 metastatic melanomas and matched germline DNA in 2012.

claim: The authors identified PREX2 as a significantly mutated gene (SMG) in the population of 25 metastatic melanomas.
source: The authors identified the phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate-dependent Rac exchange factor 2 gene (PREX2) as a significantly mutated gene (SMG) in this population and went on to confirm this finding in an independent cohort of 107 human melanoma samples.
evidence: The claim references findings from Berger et al., 2012.

claim: Berger et al. confirmed the PREX2 SMG finding in an independent cohort of 107 human melanoma samples.
source: The authors identified the phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate-dependent Rac exchange factor 2 gene (PREX2) as a significantly mutated gene (SMG) in this population and went on to confirm this finding in an independent cohort of 107 human melanoma samples.

claim: Six identified mutant PREX2 isoforms were ectopically expressed in immortalized human melanocytes to investigate the functional relevance of PREX2 mutations.
source: To investigate the functional relevance of PREX2 mutations, six of the identified mutant PREX2 isoforms were ectopically expressed in immortalized human melanocytes and tumor formation was monitored after injecting into immunodeficient mice.

claim: Four of the PREX2 mutations (three truncating variants and a point mutant) resulted in a statistically significant decrease in tumor-free survival compared to control melanocytes expressing wild-type PREX2 or GFP.

claim: Other studies have failed to identify PREX2 as an SMG in genome-wide screens of melanoma samples.
source: While Berger et al. (2012) reported PREX2 as an SMG in melanoma, other studies have failed to identify PREX2 as an SMG in genome-wide screens of melanoma samples (Cancer Genome Atlas Network, 2015; Hodis et al., 2012; Krauthammer et al., 2012; Marzese et al., 2014; Ni et al., 2013), including a meta-analysis of over 200 samples (Xia et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to other studies.

claim: A meta-analysis of over 200 melanoma samples failed to identify PREX2 as an SMG.
